Rules:
- One commitment per line.

- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.

# Summary of a 2010 UK General Election Manifesto

This manifesto was published during the 2010 UK general election, addressing several key challenges: economic recovery following the global financial crisis, political reform after the parliamentary expenses scandal, and ongoing military operations abroad.

## Economic Policy

The document prioritises securing economic recovery while halving the budget deficit over four years through a combination of growth, targeted spending cuts to lower-priority programmes, and tax measures on higher earners. Major proposals include banking reform to prevent future crises, creating public investment funds for growing businesses, and developing a high-tech industrial strategy with emphasis on green industries. Infrastructure investment features prominently, including high-speed rail and universal broadband access.

## Public Services

The manifesto commits to protecting frontline spending on healthcare, education, policing, and childcare. In healthcare, it proposes legally binding patient guarantees on waiting times and cancer care, expanded preventative medicine, and greater patient choice. Education priorities include early years expansion, one-to-one tuition for struggling pupils, and raising the education leaving age to eighteen.

## Social Policy

Key social measures include maintaining the minimum wage with increases linked to average earnings, reforming welfare to require work participation while ensuring employment always pays more than benefits, and creating a National Care Service for elderly care with protection against catastrophic care costs. First-time homebuyers would receive stamp duty exemptions.

## Political Reform

In response to public distrust, the manifesto proposes referenda on electoral reform (Alternative Vote) and an elected second chamber, fixed-term parliaments, a statutory register of lobbyists, and exploration of a written constitution.

## International Affairs

The document affirms commitment to military operations in Afghanistan while proposing a Strategic Defence Review. It supports continued engagement with international institutions and commits to spending 0.7% of national income on overseas aid.
